summary: An Indologist who studied under Paul Thieme, Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin (attested 1982–1994) and served as a project leader and editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989, 2008).

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at Nagasaki University (~1984–2004) and founded the Japan Association for Bioethics and Earth System and Ethics Association.
Haruka Yanagisawa was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at Chiba University (~1976–1996) and the University of Tokyo (~1996–2007).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, Harumi Hirano Ziegler earned an MA and a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, completing her doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2001.

Harunaga Isaacson, an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Groningen and Leiden University. He held positions at the University of Oxford (1995–2000), University of Pennsylvania (2002–2006), and University of Hamburg (2000–2002; professor from 2006).

Linguist Harushige Kōzu studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo, as well as at Balliol College and the University of Oxford. He held teaching posts at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and Musashi University (from 1968).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Harvey B. Aronson completed his doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2001).

Harvey Paul Alper worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (~1968–1976) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Southern Methodist University from 1974 to 1987.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia studied under Henry Heras and under F. J. Richards at University College London. He served as professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1945–1946).

Haya Akegarasu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He founded Seishinkai and served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954).
Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London under D. C. Lau, as well as under Nicole Vandier-Nicolas and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Heeraman Tiwari, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at the universities of Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held positions at JNU, Heidelberg University (2011–2012), and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2014–2015).
Hege Myrlund Larsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Bergen under the supervision of Bruce Kapferer (attested 2009).
Hegoda Khemananda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya (both attested 1993).

Heidi Fjeld is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Oxford and earned her doctoral degree at the University of Oslo under Signe Howell (~2001–2006), later serving there as a postdoctoral fellow (~2006–2010).

Heidi I. Koppl works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under Sherab Zangpo.

Indologist Heidi R. M. Pauwels studied at KU Leuven and the University of Washington under Alan Entwistle. She was a lecturer at SOAS (1994–1996) and became South Asian Program Coordinator (1996) and Professor (2002) at the University of Washington.

Indologist Heike Oberlin earned degrees from the University of Tübingen and the University of Würzburg. She held positions at Tübingen from 2005, becoming Associate Professor (~2013), and served as a visiting scholar at Kerala Kalamandalam and Sapienza University of Rome.

Indologist and art historian Heimo Rau earned his PhD at the University of Vienna. He worked at the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin (1938–1945), directed several Goethe-Institut branches, and taught Indian art and archaeology at Heidelberg University (1966–1982).

Hein Htet Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Edinburgh Napier University, Yangon University of Economics, James Cook University, and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University. In 2024, he served as Director of Australasia for Atheist Alliance International.
